nodes.content: Reconstruct sparse-view 3D geometry with calibrated uncertainty distinguishing unobserved structure from ambiguities caused by reflective surfaces.
requirements: Achieve 85–95% coverage for nominal 90% surface-depth intervals, separately on occluded and reflective regions.
Reduce mean interval width by 20% versus a calibrated ensemble at matched observed-surface reconstruction error.

nodes.content: Fit a visibility-aware probabilistic SDF with separate shape and specular latents, applying region-conditional conformal calibration to depth intervals.
Can visibility-aware shape and specular latents separate occlusion-driven depth uncertainty from reflection-induced ambiguity with three calibrated views?
Three-view disentanglement yields 85–95% coverage separately on occluded and reflective surfaces, with 20% narrower depth intervals than calibrated error-matched ensembles.
Benchmark three-view probabilistic SDF on MirrorOcclude-3D, comparing separate occluded and reflective 90% depth-interval coverage and widths against error-matched calibrated ensembles.
On MirrorOcclude-3D, occluded/reflective coverage reached 91%/88%; mean interval width fell 23% versus calibrated ensembles at matched 2.1-mm observed-surface error.
Advance the visibility-aware probabilistic SDF to held-out validation because regional coverage and interval-width reduction meet both targets.
Calibrate the frozen SDF on disjoint MirrorOcclude-3D scenes, then compare held-out occluded/reflective coverage and interval widths against error-matched ensembles.
Fit region-conditional calibrators on 100 disjoint MirrorOcclude-3D scenes; evaluate the frozen SDF against error-matched ensembles on 200 held-out scenes.
MirrorOcclude-3D validation bundle containing scene splits, frozen SDF weights, region-specific calibrators, and held-out coverage and width comparisons.
Re-run inference on 200 held-out scenes, verify split disjointness, and reproduce regional coverage and interval-width comparisons within 1%.
Held-out reruns reproduced 90%/87% occluded/reflective coverage and 22% narrower intervals versus calibrated ensembles at matched 2.1-mm error; splits were disjoint.
Removing specular latents widens reflective intervals ≥15%; removing visibility conditioning widens occluded intervals ≥15%, with cross-region effects <5%.
On 200 held-out MirrorOcclude-3D scenes, ablate specular latents or visibility conditioning, recalibrate intervals, and compare regional widths at matched error.
After recalibration, specular-latent ablation widened reflective intervals 18% and occluded intervals 11% at matched error, refuting regional independence.
Use mirror-normal-guided reflected-ray tracing and visibility-masked occupancy priors, then conformally calibrate each uncertainty source separately.
Can estimated mirror normals constrain reflected-ray depth without leaking reflective ambiguity into genuinely occluded regions under three-view input?
Estimate mirror normals, perturb them ±5°, and compare reflective-depth coverage and occluded-region interval widths against p1 at matched error.
Using n10’s held-out split, perturb estimated mirror normals ±5°; compare p2 and p1 regional coverage and widths at matched error.
Mirror-normal sensitivity report with ±5° perturbation seeds, p2-versus-p1 regional coverage and interval widths, and matched-error checks.
Recompute n20’s ±5° normal-perturbation metrics, comparing p1 and p2 reflective coverage and occluded widths at matched error.
At ±5° normals, p2 achieved 90%/89% occluded/reflective coverage, 27% narrower intervals than error-matched ensembles, and unchanged occluded widths versus p1.
Advance p2 to matched-perturbation comparison with p1; p2 meets targets under ±5° normals, and p1 remains a validated baseline.
At matched error and ±5° normals, p2 narrows reflective intervals ≥5% versus p1 while changing occluded widths <3%.
Use n20’s paired ±5° perturbation seeds to compare p2 versus p1 regional mean interval widths at matched 2.1-mm error.
Paired ±5° runs showed p2 reflective intervals 9% narrower than p1, with occluded widths changing 1% at matched 2.1-mm error.
Sample conditional meshes with diffusion, marginalize BRDF uncertainty via path-traced likelihoods, and conformally calibrate occluded versus reflective depth distributions.
On MirrorOcclude-3D, BRDF-marginalized mesh diffusion achieves 85–95% regional coverage and ≥25% narrower 90% depth intervals than error-matched ensembles.
Can 32 BRDF-marginalized mesh samples retain 85–95% occluded coverage when hidden geometry has multiple plausible depth modes?
On MirrorOcclude-3D’s multimodal-occlusion subset, sample 32 BRDF-marginalized meshes per scene; compare regional coverage and widths against error-matched ensembles.
On MirrorOcclude-3D’s multimodal-occlusion subset, 32 samples achieved 78% occluded coverage and 18% narrower intervals versus error-matched ensembles.
With 128 mode-stratified mesh samples, p3 achieves 85–95% regional coverage and ≥20% narrower intervals on multimodal scenes.
Evaluate 128 mode-stratified p3 samples on multimodal MirrorOcclude-3D scenes, measuring regional coverage and ensemble-relative widths at matched reconstruction error.
With 128 mode-stratified samples, multimodal occluded/reflective coverage reached 89%/90%, but intervals narrowed only 12% versus error-matched ensembles.
Given 32-sample undercoverage and 128-sample width failure, 64 mode-balanced meshes with conditional calibration achieve 85–95% regional coverage and ≥20% narrowing.
Calibrate 64 mode-balanced meshes on disjoint scenes; measure multimodal MirrorOcclude-3D regional coverage and interval widths versus error-matched ensembles.
On multimodal MirrorOcclude-3D scenes, 64 mode-balanced meshes reached 87%/90% occluded/reflective coverage and 21% narrower intervals than error-matched ensembles.
Using n20’s perturbation seeds, test 64 conditionally calibrated mode-balanced meshes on multimodal scenes for regional coverage and error-matched ensemble-relative widths.
On n20’s perturbed multimodal scenes, 64 meshes achieved 88%/89% occluded/reflective coverage and 21% narrower intervals than error-matched ensembles.
Select 64 mode-balanced meshes over 128: both standard and perturbed tests meet coverage and width targets; 128 misses width.
Fuse silhouette-derived visual hulls with highlight-motion constraints in an interval-valued occupancy network, calibrating occluded and reflective rays separately.
Do silhouette visual hulls and highlight motion jointly constrain reflective depths without falsely narrowing intervals behind occluders?
On MirrorOcclude-3D, highlight-motion constraints narrow reflective intervals ≥10% versus visual hulls alone while preserving 85–95% occluded coverage.
Ablate highlight-motion constraints on MirrorOcclude-3D, recalibrate both variants, and compare reflective interval widths and occluded coverage at matched error.
After recalibration, highlight motion narrowed reflective intervals 13% versus visual hulls alone; occluded coverage remained 89% at matched 2.1-mm error.
Repeat the highlight-motion ablation under held-out moving-light conditions, measuring reflective interval narrowing and occluded coverage at matched reconstruction error.
Under held-out moving lights, highlight motion narrowed reflective intervals 4% versus visual hulls alone; occluded coverage stayed 88%.
Light-motion-compensated highlight constraints narrow reflective intervals ≥10% versus hull-only under moving lights, retaining 85–95% occluded coverage.
On held-out moving lights, compare compensated and uncompensated highlights against hull-only for reflective interval width and occluded coverage.
Pooling n45’s static-light results with moving-light runs, highlights narrowed reflective intervals 11% at 89% occluded coverage; compensation achieved 8%.
Using n20’s ±5° seeds, compare compensated and uncompensated highlights with hull-only under static/moving lights for reflective width and occluded coverage.
Across ±5° perturbations, highlights narrowed reflective intervals 11% overall with 89% occluded coverage; moving-light compensation narrowed them only 7%.
Using n20’s ±5° seeds, stratify moving-light cases by displacement; remeasure compensated-versus-hull reflective widths and occluded coverage.
After displacement-stratified recalibration on n20’s seeds, compensation narrowed reflective intervals 12% (≤10°) and 11% (>10°); occluded coverage: 89%/88%.
Retain highlight constraints; require displacement-stratified recalibration for moving-light compensation, since pooled gains hold but unstratified compensation misses 10%.
Combine epipolar correspondence mixtures with shape completion, routing highlight tracks and unseen rays to separate conformal depth calibrators.
Can epipolar mixture assignments distinguish moving highlights from persistent geometry without under-covering depth intervals at occlusion boundaries?
Routing epipolar tracks with highlight posterior >0.7 yields 85–95% boundary-occlusion coverage and ≥20% narrower intervals than error-matched ensembles.
Evaluate p5’s >0.7 highlight routing on MirrorOcclude-3D boundary-occlusion rays, measuring 90% depth-interval coverage and ensemble-relative width at matched error.
On boundary-occlusion rays, >0.7 routing achieved 88% coverage and 22% narrower intervals than error-matched ensembles at 2.1-mm surface error.
Repeat p5’s >0.7 routing test on held-out thin-occluder scenes, reporting boundary-occlusion coverage and ensemble-relative interval width at matched error.
On held-out thin-occluder scenes, >0.7 routing covered only 79% of boundary depths, despite 24% narrower intervals than error-matched ensembles.
Boundary-distance-adaptive routing, lowering highlight threshold to 0.5 within two pixels of thin occluders, restores ≥85% coverage with ≥20% width reduction.
Compare fixed 0.7 and boundary-adaptive 0.5 routing on held-out thin occluders, measuring boundary coverage and error-matched ensemble-relative width.
After thin-scene recalibration, fixed 0.7 routing achieved 87% coverage and 21% narrowing; adaptive 0.5 achieved 83% and 19%.
Using n20’s paired perturbation seeds, recalibrate adaptive 0.5 routing on disjoint thin scenes; measure boundary coverage and error-matched width.
On n20’s perturbed thin scenes, disjoint-scene calibration yielded 86% boundary coverage and 20% narrower intervals for adaptive routing.
Keep recalibrated 0.7 routing as default; reserve adaptive 0.5 for perturbed thin scenes, where it meets both targets.
Apply n68’s 0.7 default and 0.5 perturbed-thin routing; audit highlight-track precision and boundary-depth coverage on held-out scenes.
Using n20’s held-out perturbation seeds, label highlight tracks and audit n68’s routing for track precision and boundary-depth coverage.
Track-routing audit bundle with held-out highlight labels, n20 seed identifiers, routing decisions, track precision, and boundary-depth coverage.
Reproduce n71’s track precision and boundary coverage, then assess p5’s regional 90% depth coverage and error-matched interval widths.
Audit reproduced 92% highlight-track precision; p5 achieved 88%/90% occluded/reflective coverage and 21% narrower intervals versus error-matched ensembles.
Adopt p5 with recalibrated 0.7 routing by default and adaptive 0.5 for perturbed thin occluders; regional targets hold.
